title: Masela language - Wikipedia
text: Masela is the language of Marsela Island in southern Maluku, Indonesia. Regional varieties are distinct; Ethnologue counts it as three languages.

title: Masela, West | Ethnologue Free
text: West Masela is an endangered indigenous language of Indonesia. It belongs to the Austronesian language family. Direct evidence is lacking, but the language is thought to be used as a first language by adults only.

title: West Masela - mss (Austronesian) - PeopleGroups.org
text: West Masela (mss) is part of the Austronesian family and Austronesian, Malayo-Polynesian, Central-Eastern Malayo-Polynesian, Babar, South, Masela-South Babar class.

title: Masela language
text: West Masela is associated with five villages, including Nura in Masela District, where the language remains a key marker of identity amid interactions with neighboring Babar speakers, though usage is low (e.g., 40% among adults in some contexts).
